target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (L : Language.{0}) [L.DecidableEq] [L.ReferenceableBy L] (T₀ T : Theory L)
    [Diagonalization T₀] [T₀ ⪯ T] (𝔅 : Provability T₀ T) [𝔅.HBL],
    (∀ σ : Sentence L, T ⊢ (𝔅 σ 🡒 σ)) → Entailment.Inconsistent T
translation: Target is the proposition stating that for every first-order language L (in universe 0) that has decidable equality of symbols and Gödel numerals for its own sentences, for every pair of theories (sets of sentences) T₀ and T in L such that T₀ satisfies the diagonalization lemma (every formula θ(x) has a sentence γ with T₀ ⊢ γ 🡘 θ(⌜γ⌝)) and every theorem of T₀ is a theorem of T, and for every provability predicate 𝔅 for T over T₀ (a formula of L satisfying derivability condition D1: whenever T ⊢ σ, T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 σ) that also satisfies derivability conditions D2 (T₀ ⊢ 𝔅(σ 🡒 τ) 🡒 𝔅 σ 🡒 𝔅 τ) and D3 (T₀ ⊢ 𝔅 σ 🡒 𝔅(𝔅 σ)): if, for every sentence σ of L, T derives the formal implication 𝔅 σ 🡒 σ, then T is inconsistent (derives every sentence). Note that L is not required to be the language of arithmetic, T₀ and T are not required to be recursively enumerable or Δ₁-presented, 𝔅 is not required to be a standard provability predicate or to define a recursively enumerable set, and the reflection hypothesis T ⊢ (𝔅 σ 🡒 σ) is required to hold for all sentences σ of L.

divergences.description: Relative to P-C2, the Lean theorem weakens the result by assuming the full local reflection schema (∀ σ, T ⊢ 𝔅 σ 🡒 σ) rather than only consistency (T ⊢ ∼𝔅 ⊥, Chalmers's premise (4)), which also makes the HBL conditions D2 and D3 ([𝔅.HBL]) mathematically redundant (since the Gödel-sentence instance alone yields inconsistency from D1 and diagonalization). However, this choice directly matches P-C2b's claim about knowing soundness rather than merely consistency.

The Lean cannot express 'the system knows it is sound' as a single internal sentence about semantic truth (there is no truth predicate or intended model in an arbitrary language L); instead it formalizes soundness disquotationally via an external universal quantifier over all sentences (the local reflection schema).

Chalmers's informal epistemic notions of 'knowledge', 'unassailable assertion' (|-), and 'belief' (B) are idealized as classical first-order derivability (T ⊢) from a theory T and a syntactic formula 𝔅 (imposing classical first-order deductive closure, though faithfully avoiding any computability/RE assumption). Correspondingly, 'leads to a contradiction' is rendered as object-level inconsistency (Entailment.Inconsistent T) rather than a meta-level contradiction via factivity of knowledge (though classically equivalent to the impossibility of a consistent system proving local reflection).

Rather than a single system with the resources of Peano arithmetic (and only the single diagonal sentence G ↔ ¬B(G)), the Lean generalizes by quantifying universally over any universe-0 language L with decidable equality and Gödel numbering ([L.ReferenceableBy L]) and any pair of theories T₀ ⪯ T where T₀ satisfies full diagonalization; this is a harmless strengthening since taking T₀ = T recovers the single-system case.

judgement.summary: The Lean statement faithfully captures Chalmers's claim that a (not necessarily computable) system asserting its own soundness under Chalmers's belief and diagonalization conditions must be inconsistent. Its caveats are minor formalization choices: encoding 'knows it is sound' via the external local reflection schema in classical first-order logic (which is stronger than P-C2's consistency-only premise (4) and renders D2–D3 redundant) and abstracting Peano arithmetic to an arbitrary diagonalizable base theory T₀ ⪯ T.
